parole.significato: sighthound (a hound that primarily hunts by sight and speed, instead of by scent and endurance)
parole.testo: From Old Hungarian agar and earlier Agar. Borrowed from a West Slavic language. Compare Czech ohař, Polish ogar and Slovak ohar, from Proto-Slavic *ogarь. A direct borrowing from a (Oghuric) Turkic language is less likely. First attested in 1193.

parole.significato: cube (regular polyhedron having six identical square faces)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a West Slavic language, probably from Czech or Slovak. Compare Czech kostka, Slovak kocka.
Borrowed from a West Slavic language. Compare Czech and Slovak chorý.

parole.significato: a covered edifice with open sideways
parole.testo: Borrowed from a West Slavic or East Slavic language. Compare Slovak sieň (“hall”).
Back-formation from sántál (“to limp, hobble”), a verb used in the Székely dialect, from a West Slavic or East Slavic language, ultimately from Proto-Slavic *šętati.
